metadata.title: RAGfly — Multi-tenant RAG service for AI agents
metadata.description: Multi-tenant RAG service for AI agents, with per-context isolation and verifiable privacy for each deployment mode. Connect a directory via MCP, REST, CLI or SDK.

hero.slogan: Simple, private, and precise. And each of your contexts, in its own space.
hero.lineaApoyo: Works with the agents you already use — over MCP — and with the ones you build.
hero.tagline: Any agent conversing with thousands of private documents: at scale and isolated per context. Connect a directory and your agent answers with citations — without building or maintaining a RAG pipeline.

construyendo.descripcion: Consume it from wherever you work — MCP, REST, CLI or SDK. The document context layer comes solved; you build the agent logic.
construyendo.cardATitulo: I'm building an agent for one client
construyendo.cardADesc: You have a large corpus and don't want to build or maintain the RAG pipeline. Point RAGfly at the directory and build the agent logic, not the pipeline.
construyendo.cardBTitulo: I deploy agents for many clients
construyendo.cardBDesc: You serve many and need each one's corpus kept isolated. Multi-tenant out of the box, governed from a single panel.
construyendo.cardCTitulo: I'm adding RAG to my SaaS
construyendo.cardCDesc: You don't want to rebuild ingestion, scale, multi-tenancy and security. RAGfly gives it to you solved, consumed via MCP, REST, CLI or SDK.

problema.titulo1: The RAG that works with 1,000 documents
problema.descripcion: Almost all software will carry AI agents, and almost all of those agents need to talk to private documents: contracts, case files, regulations, records, manuals. That's where everyone hits the same wall: solving ingestion, vectorization, freshness, isolation between clients and auditing at scale becomes an infrastructure project in itself — expensive, slow and easy to get wrong.
problema.sin0: Assemble vector DB + parser + framework + your own security layer
problema.sin1: Build multi-client isolation by hand (and pray it doesn't leak)
problema.sin2: Upload the documents to a third-party cloud
problema.sin3: Lock yourself into a vector DB or LLM vendor
problema.sin4: Months of integration before the first result
problema.con0: Point at a directory; ingestion, vectorization and indexing are automatic
problema.con1: Multi-tenant out of the box: an isolated corpus per context, from the database up
problema.con2: Cloud does not retain the original; Desktop processes it locally; on sovereign plans the database belongs to the customer
problema.con3: DB-agnostic and BYO: bring your own vector database and your own model
problema.con4: From zero to an agent answering with citations with no integration project

queEs.descripcion: Point RAGfly at a directory of documents — thousands or tens of thousands, scanned ones included — and get a secure, multi-tenant, production-ready retrieval foundation. Retrieval at scale, isolation between clients and data governance come solved. You focus on your agent's logic; RAGfly is the ground it stands on.
queEs.bullet0: Pointing is your whole job — governing many clients doesn't cost you an engineering project
queEs.bullet1: Text, tables, layout and scans: PDF, Word, Excel, plain text
queEs.bullet2: Production-ready from the very first directory

combina.item0Desc: An isolated corpus per context, governed from a single panel with a Groups → Entities → Areas structure. Serve 20 contexts from one platform without a single piece of data crossing from one to another. It's what cloud-first context engines don't solve: there, you build that isolation yourself.
combina.item1Titulo: Precise privacy for each deployment mode
combina.item1Desc: RAGfly processes both ingestion and retrieval. Cloud processes the original file but does not retain it after ingestion. Desktop processes the original and extraction inside your network and may synchronize encrypted derivatives. On sovereign plans, the customer owns the database and derivatives at rest, while RAGfly accesses chunks to retrieve context.
combina.item2Desc: No integration project. Ingestion, vectorization and indexing are automatic, at the scale of tens of thousands of files. Your only job is to point; the system handles the rest.
combina.capaTitulo: And the layer underneath — where the value lives
combina.capaDesc: Retrieval intelligence, not just storage: reranking, hybrid search, adaptive chunking, freshness, permission filtering and citation accuracy. It's what the agent can't do on its own — it can't see inside the corpus. And an action layer, not just a context layer: the agent invokes operations over sets of documents by prompt, not just retrieving chunks.

chat.eyebrow: Try it by talking to it
chat.descripcion: RAGfly has a chat that isn't for "chatting with your files" — it's for operating the platform by talking to it. Add a user, create a profile, change someone's area or request support, all from the same place. Need a token? Ask how and it takes you to the form. Change a user's area? It does it, or opens the screen for you.
chat.descripcion2: And yes, you can also query your documents and test retrieval before integrating anything. It's the fastest way to see the value without writing code — before writing a line of code.
chat.nota: A DX test, not the product: the chat uses every primitive, but the focus is on the infrastructure.
chat.demo0: add ana@client.com to the Finance area
chat.demo0r: User created. Inherits the "Finance Analyst" profile.
chat.demo1: summarize the contracts expiring this month
chat.demo1r: 3 contracts · cited to their source file
chat.demo2: give me an MCP token for my agent
chat.demo2r: Done. Opening the credentials form for you.

identidades.titulo1: You don't give your agent access to the documents.
identidades.descripcion: In RAGfly, everyone who queries is an identity with permissions. An identity can be a person (signs in with their email) or a profile: a reusable service identity, with a blind code and no personal data behind it.
identidades.p0: The agent comes in as "Finance Analyst" and sees exactly what that profile would see — its area, its level, its entity — with the same rules an employee would have. The RBAC that protects people protects agents just the same: the finance agent doesn't touch HR or another company in the holding.
identidades.p1: You define the profile once and assign it to any agent, today or next year. For a consultancy deploying agents for 20 clients, that's 20 isolated sets of profiles, governed from a single place. It's the answer to the number-one fear of anyone putting an agent into a regulated organization: that it leaks a document it shouldn't have seen.
identidades.tag2: Same RBAC for people and agents

modos.descripcion: Same interface. In Cloud, RAGfly processes the original and relevant chunks. On Desktop, the local component processes the original inside your network and keeps it out of RAGfly Cloud.
modos.cloudDesc: Get going right away, with no infrastructure of your own. RAGfly provisions everything and you point at your directory.
modos.desktopDesc: The original and its extraction are processed inside your network. Derivatives may be synchronized, and RAGfly processes chunks during retrieval.
modos.desktop0: The original file does not reach RAGfly Cloud
modos.desktop2: Hands your agent each file's local path, not a copy — it opens the file where it lives
modos.nota: Desktop doesn't replace your agent — Claude Code, whichever you use: it serves it better. It's the same RAGfly action layer, more powerful when it runs inside your network.

download.descripcion: RAGfly's local component: point it at your files directory and it scans, vectorizes and indexes them automatically. The original and its extraction are processed inside your network; only encrypted derivatives are uploaded to the cloud.
download.notaInstalacion: macOS: the first time, right-click the app → Open. Windows: if SmartScreen warns you, More info → Run anyway.
download.paso0Desc: Graphical installers: DMG on macOS, wizard on Windows. No terminal, no dependencies.
download.paso1Desc: With your RAGfly account. Your group, your spaces and your permissions travel with you.
download.paso2Desc: RAGfly scans, vectorizes and indexes your documents, ready for your interface and your agents.
download.cloudNota: Prefer to start without installing anything?
download.actualizacion: Updates download on their own: when a new version is ready, just hit «Restart to apply».

superficies.tituloAccent: Use it from wherever you work.
superficies.descripcion: Four surfaces, on every plan. The message is one of neutrality; the path we show first is MCP.
superficies.mcpDesc: Connect RAGfly as an MCP server and your agent converses with the documents without you building any UI. It's where we open the door.
superficies.restDesc: The universal production foundation. The base everything else sits on.
superficies.cliDesc: DX, operations and bulk ingestion. Day-to-day convenience.
superficies.sdkDesc: Integrate RAGfly directly into your code. Python and TypeScript. No MCP infrastructure required.
superficies.accionDesc: The agent doesn't stop at retrieving chunks: it invokes operations over sets of documents by prompt, from your own agent.
superficies.accionCita: «Download these 500 documents and put them where I tell you.»
superficies.accionRemate: RAGfly is a toolset of document operations that the agent calls, not just a context provider.
superficies.planesNota: All six interfaces —web chat, MCP, REST, Python SDK, TypeScript SDK and CLI— are on every plan, the free one included. RAGfly Desktop is separate, from Starter up.

construido.item0Desc: Postgres + pgvector (Supabase to get started) + embeddings. A dedicated vector DB stays as a scale option, and you can always bring your own (BYO vector database + BYO LLM).
construido.item1Desc: Each document's state lives in a relational database on Postgres: mixed SQL + vector queries inside your network, without a closed API in a third party's cloud.
construido.item2Desc: Text, tables, layout and messy scans (PDF, Word, Excel, plain text). Deliberate scope on text + OCR, no audio or video.
construido.item3Desc: Four levels — System, Group, Entity, User — where the lowest overrides the one above. The logic is configured with prompts that the engine compiles into behavior.

seguridad.descripcion: Protection is a design pillar, not a premium plan. Confidential documents stay under your organization's control.
seguridad.punto0: Cloud processes the original file but does not retain it after ingestion; chunks, embeddings and metadata persist
seguridad.punto1: Document data encrypted at rest in the database
seguridad.punto2: Structural filtering from the database up: every access goes through views that filter what each identity can see
seguridad.punto3: Full isolation between organizations: no group sees another's data
seguridad.punto4: Granular RBAC by area, role and profile — the same for people and agents
seguridad.punto5: Internal operation only through validated APIs: no surface for prompt injection
seguridad.punto6: Two-factor authentication and secure JWT tokens
seguridad.punto7: Full audit trail: every action logged with identity, date and module
seguridad.punto9: Desktop processes the original locally; on sovereign plans the customer owns the database and derivatives at rest, while RAGfly accesses chunks to retrieve context

quickstart.heroTitle1: From zero to your first result
quickstart.heroDesc: RAGfly exposes four integration surfaces. Pick the one that fits your workflow — the result is the same: your agent or application answering with citations from your documents.
quickstart.apiKeyTitle: Before you start — get your API Key
quickstart.apiKeyDesc: Go to <link>app.ragfly.ai/api-keys</link> and create a key with the role you need. You'll see it only once — save it in your secrets manager.
quickstart.apiKeyRole1: DOC-ADMIN — read and write (documents, workspaces, skills)
quickstart.mcpDesc: The fastest path if you already use an MCP-compatible LLM agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, etc.). The agent discovers tools automatically — no integration code to write.
quickstart.mcpStep1Title: Add RAGfly as an MCP server
quickstart.mcpStep1HttpNote: If your client supports streamable HTTP (more efficient): use <c>https://api.ragfly.ai/mcp-http/</c>
quickstart.mcpStep2Title: Restart your client and verify the connection
quickstart.mcpStep2Note: Tools appear with prefix <c>mcp__ragfly__</c>. Call first:
quickstart.restDesc: Direct access from any language or platform. Base URL: <c>https://api.ragfly.ai</c> · Interactive Swagger: <link>api.ragfly.ai/docs</link>
quickstart.restEp6: Execute skill on workspace or doc
quickstart.cliDesc: Ideal for scripts, automations, CI/CD pipelines, and terminal operation. No need to write HTTP directly.
quickstart.ctaDesc: Start free — no card, no friction.
quickstart.pathSdkDesc: Native Python, no MCP infrastructure needed
quickstart.sdkDesc: The official RAGfly Python SDK. Two main methods: ask() for full RAG and search() for pure retrieval. Supports streaming and context manager.

build.metaDesc: Connect your agent or app to RAGfly: six interfaces (MCP, Python SDK, TypeScript SDK, REST, CLI, Web), one auth contract, RBAC by design. Docs for Claude, Codex, developers and consultancies.

build.apiKeyTitle: Before you start — get your API Key
build.apiKeyDesc: The group admin creates a key at app.ragfly.ai/api-keys (or via POST /auth/api-key). Shown only once — store it in a secrets manager.
build.webDesc: End users operate at app.ragfly.ai directly — no integration needed.
build.rawDesc: Every doc is also served as plain Markdown so an agent can fetch it directly. Point your agent at:

negativa.descripcion: A verifier breaks the answer into claims and checks each one against its evidence before showing it. If something isn't backed, it doesn't ship.
negativa.nota: You can only trust a system that knows how to say no.
negativa.item2: citation resolved to document and page
negativa.respuesta: I found no evidence in your documents to answer this with confidence.
negativa.pie: Every claim that does pass the check comes with its citation, linking straight to the document and the page.

simple.descripcion: You bring the directory —a local folder or Google Drive— and the system loads, extracts, analyzes, chunks and vectorizes on its own. No document ingestion to build, no upfront configuration and no integration project.
simple.formatos: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF, plain text and scans via OCR.
simple.ritmoTitulo: The climb is slow; the cruise is steady.
simple.ritmoDesc: Ingesting a large corpus is an unattended process: you leave it running. Where speed matters —the query at runtime— is where you get it. Nobody minds a long boarding; everybody minds a late flight.
simple.onboardingDesc: If you start out alone, group, entity, area and profile are a single node that unfolds as your organization grows. The simplicity of day one, with the enterprise ceiling already built in.
simple.interfacesDesc: Web chat, MCP server, REST API /v1, Python SDK, TypeScript SDK and CLI: one configuration feeds them all. RAGfly Desktop is separate, from Starter up.
simple.limiteDesc: Audio and video are out of scope, by focus. We'd rather say it up front.

privado.titulo1: We never store your document in the cloud.
privado.tituloAccent: And if you want, the document never leaves your network.
privado.descripcion: In Cloud the original is processed on the way in and not retained: what persists are the derivatives —chunks, embeddings and metadata—. With Desktop, the file and its extraction stay inside your network, and depending on the deployment encrypted derivatives may be synchronized. On sovereign plans, that database is yours.
privado.manifiestoTitulo: It's not that you can't see it. It's that it isn't on board.
privado.manifiestoDesc: The group and entity filter lives inside the SQL search function itself: vectors from another context are never even scored. It isn't a filter applied afterwards — they never entered the search. It holds on every plan, the free one included.
privado.subeTitulo: Uploading vectorized content is not uploading the document.
privado.subeDesc: Extracted text goes up, in chunks, encrypted. The file doesn't. If the document is signed, the signature doesn't go up.
privado.cartaDesc: The group is the tenant; the entity separates organizations or contexts within the group; the area defines which document subtree each identity sees, with hierarchical inheritance — whoever sits above sees what their descendant areas hold.
privado.cartaCierre: With no area assigned, access is closed by default, never open. The text of a forbidden document never reaches the model or the agent: it isn't hidden on screen, it doesn't enter the prompt.
privado.byokTitulo: No model under our account ever sees your document.
privado.byokDesc: With parsing-BYOK and embedding-BYOK the five pipeline calls —reading, typing, summary, attributes and vectorization— run on your credentials, against Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, under your contract and your invoice.
privado.byokNota: And if your credential fails —quota, rate limit, provider down—, the operation fails and we tell you: we never retry with ours. A silent fallback would break exactly that promise.
privado.pisoTitulo: Set by the plan, not by a checkbox.
privado.pisoDesc: Paid plans resolve only against model providers contractually bound not to train on the content sent — not a checkbox someone can leave in the wrong position.
privado.pisoVerificacion: Verified by an automated suite that mirrors the resolution across all 462 plan × skill combinations, with a positive control.
privado.pisoHonestidad: The free plan runs on low-cost models that don't include that clause: it's for evaluation, not for sensitive documents. We'd rather say it up front.
privado.pildora0: AES-256-GCM · application-level encryption with key hierarchy

preciso.tituloAccent: and shows where it came from.
preciso.descripcion: The answer doesn't end at the text: it ends at the exact chunk that backs it, with its page.
preciso.hibridaDesc: Three branches —vector search over pgvector, lexical search over what the system understood from the document, and a dedicated branch for the summary— fused and reordered by a multilingual reranker.
preciso.degradacionNota: If rerank isn't available, the degradation is visible, not silent.
preciso.citasTitulo: Direct link to the document and the page
preciso.citasDesc: Every claim carries its citation. The trail runs from the answer to the chunk that backs it, and you can follow it.
preciso.evalDesc: An evaluation suite with verifiable ground truth: the question is generated from the real chunk that answers it, so the correct answer is known in advance.

config.descripcion: Everything you configure becomes context your agent receives — editable from the screen, with no deploy and no developer. It's what separates RAGfly from a vector database with a chat on top.
config.card0Desc: Product → application → function → your business hierarchy (group, entity, area, profile) → capability catalog. You write «this group is a construction company; its documents are usually works contracts» and from the next message on, everyone answers through that lens.
config.card0Nota: A change in a text box, new behavior instantly.
config.card1Desc: The pipeline doesn't chunk blindly: it types each document and extracts only the attributes that apply to its type —amount, counterparty, due date—.
config.card1Nota: That's what enables exact answers: «how many invoices from May?», «the contract with the highest amount».
config.card2Desc: Before vectorizing, each chunk is prefixed with the whole document's record: name, location, date, summary and attributes. Enrichment, not just chunking.
config.card2Nota: It's measured: we tried removing it and retrieval got worse. The summary also competes as a candidate of its own in the search.

perfiles.titulo1: You don't give your agent access to the documents.
perfiles.descripcion: The agent signs in as «Finance Analyst» and sees exactly what that profile would see — under the same access rules as your people.
perfiles.p0Desc: A profile is an identity with no personal data, designed for agents. It inherits the same machinery as a person: area with hierarchical inheritance, associated locations, roles, RBAC and identity prompts. No master keys.
perfiles.p1Desc: Group, entity and area are pinned: not even the agent itself can ask for a different context.
perfiles.p2Desc: The credential is issued in the name of an identity and inherits its scope: change the profile's area and what the agent sees changes, without touching the integration.
perfiles.p3Desc: Twenty contexts are twenty isolated sets of profiles, governed from a single place. You define the profile once and assign it to any agent, today or next year.
perfiles.remate: It's the answer to the number one fear of anyone deploying an agent inside a regulated organization: that it leaks someone a document they weren't supposed to see.

lockin.descripcion: The database and the model are interchangeable inputs — the value is in the governed engine.
lockin.card0Desc: With parsing-BYOK and embedding-BYOK, processing runs on your credentials, against Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, under your contract and your invoice.
lockin.card1Desc: Vectors can live in your own database instead of ours: on Scale, your own Supabase —the same engine that runs RAGfly, Postgres with pgvector—; on Enterprise, other engines.
lockin.card2Desc: Your corpus is exportable: what goes in can come back out.
lockin.remate: Your models never see the document and your vectors live on your infrastructure.

cierre.titulo: Point RAGfly at your documents and give any agent the exact context it needs — production-ready and isolated by context.
cierre.northStarTitulo: We build for agents in production, not for demos.
cierre.northStarDesc: We measure what matters: agents and applications serving retrieval from RAGfly. Not chat users, not documents uploaded.
cierre.faqTitulo: What people ask us before starting

faq.a0: A RAG service for AI agents: it turns any document corpus —thousands or tens of thousands, scans included— into a secure, multi-tenant retrieval base that's ready for production, without building or maintaining a RAG pipeline.
faq.a1: For developers, consultancies and integrators building AI agents on private documents —sometimes for many different clients— who don't want to build or maintain a RAG pipeline at scale.
faq.a2: Plans in USD: Free $0, Starter $39/mo, Growth $149/mo, Scale $590/mo and Enterprise/Sovereign custom. Each plan shows its quota of Pages, Retrievals, Verified Answers and Entities, plus the available add-ons where they apply. MCP/REST/CLI/SDK surfaces on every plan.
faq.a3: You point RAGfly at your documents directory; the system scans, vectorizes and indexes them automatically. Then your agent retrieves by meaning and gets answers with citations to the source via MCP, REST or CLI, isolated by context and with the data handling that matches the deployment mode.
faq.q4: How does an AI agent consume RAGfly?
faq.a4: Through a remote MCP server (SSE or HTTP) or the RAGfly Desktop CLI, authenticating with a JWT or an API Key. The catalog of operations is published at `https://ragfly.ai/agents.json` and `https://ragfly.ai/llms-full.txt`.
faq.q5: What does RAGfly process, and where does my data end up?
faq.a5: RAGfly processes document information on the way in and relevant chunks on the way out. In Cloud it processes the original file but does not retain it after ingestion; chunks, embeddings and metadata persist. With Desktop, the original and its extraction are processed inside your network, although derivatives may be synchronized. On sovereign plans, the database and the derivatives at rest belong to the customer; RAGfly accesses the chunks it needs to retrieve and deliver context.
faq.q6: How is one customer's data isolated from another's?
faq.a6: Multi-tenant by default: each customer lives in a corpus isolated at the database level, with a Groups → Entities → Areas structure. A consultancy or integrator can serve dozens of customers from a single platform without a single record crossing over.
faq.q7: Can I use my own vector database and my own model?
faq.a7: Yes. RAGfly is DB-agnostic: on the advanced plans you bring your own vector database (BYO) and choose your own embedding and LLM models, without being tied to a provider.
faq.q8: Which AI models does it work with — Claude, GPT, Gemini?
faq.a8: RAGfly is model-agnostic. It delivers retrieval with citations and permissions; your agent runs on whichever LLM you prefer —Claude, GPT, Gemini or another— and consumes RAGfly via MCP, REST or CLI.
faq.q9: Which formats are supported? Does it work with scanned PDFs (OCR)?
faq.a9: PDF, Word, Excel and plain text, including scanned documents thanks to first-rate OCR and table and layout understanding. The focus is text and complex documents, not audio or video.
faq.q10: Can I use it with regulated data (legal, healthcare, government)?
faq.a10: Yes. Desktop processes the original file and its extraction inside the customer's network. On sovereign plans, the customer owns the database where the derivatives persist. RAGfly still processes chunks on the way out to produce retrieval; a full in-situ runtime is the mode that keeps that processing inside the customer's infrastructure too.
faq.q11: How long does it take to go from a directory to an agent answering with citations?
faq.a11: You point RAGfly at a directory and, with automatic ingestion, vectorization and indexing, you can have an agent answering with citations in a short time, with no human help — and without building or maintaining a RAG pipeline at scale.
